Peak crate labels rules
This page teaches how a new handler works

Peak crate labels rules matter because cargo moves faster when the label, documents, and booking notes match from the start. On the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, your job is to keep the intake calm, accurate, and easy for the passenger coordinator to review. Start by listening carefully, then confirm the species, crate details, and route notes before anything is accepted for travel.

For bird bookings, check the travel record before you promise space. <<FACT F077>> Keep your tone steady and plain, because travelers rely on clear guidance when they are already managing a pet and a trip. If the animal is not eligible, say so directly and move on to the next step in the intake.

For cat bookings, compare the crate measurements, fit, and service notes against the booking file. <<FACT F061>> If the crate looks oversized, damaged, or poorly secured, pause the intake and refer the matter to the senior coordinator. Do not guess, and do not let a rushed check create a loading problem later at the gate.

For reptile bookings, confirm the handling category and the required charge before you finalize the record. <<FACT F060>> Add only approved notes, keep the wording clean, and make sure the traveler understands what will appear on the itinerary. If a traveler arrives with extra paperwork, review it against the file instead of making assumptions.

Use warm professional language at every point. If Rafael Silva or Emil Cohen calls with a concern, answer in the same clear way you would use at the counter. If Trixie is listed on a booking, treat the pet record with the same care as any other live-animal entry. End every shift with the file complete, the labels readable, and the handoff ready for the next team. Remember: precise labels protect animals, travelers, and the operation.
